domains.risk_context: Unclear ownership and accountability can lead to inconsistent security decisions and outcomes degrading over time.

domains.name: Visibility and response
domains.description: Procedures and capabilities for detecting, analysing and responding to cyber security events and incidents.
domains.risk_context: Limited visibility and response can delay the detection, analysis and containment of intrusions.

domains.name: Boundary services
domains.description: Assets at network boundaries that broker connectivity between environments of different trust levels, including internet-facing services and edge devices.
domains.risk_context: Internet-facing and boundary systems are routinely exposed to adversary scanning and exploitation making them common targets for initial access.

domains.name: Identity services
domains.description: Enterprise-wide identity, credential and access management services such as directories, authentication and authorisation services or credential stores.
domains.risk_context: Compromise of enterprise-wide identity services can enable an adversary to gain persistent or privileged access across the enterprise.

domains.name: Critical processes and services
domains.description: Core processes and services that are critical to delivering primary organisational outcomes.
domains.risk_context: Compromise or loss of these systems can disrupt the organisation’s ability to deliver critical outcomes or services.

domains.name: Privileged environments
domains.description: Systems and services that support privileged activities, management services and high-impact administrative functions.
domains.risk_context: Compromise of privileged systems can give an adversary extensive control over systems, services and security controls.

domains.name: Business systems
domains.description: Supporting enterprise functions that collectively enable organisational operations.
domains.risk_context: Compromise can disrupt day-to-day operations and provide pathways to more sensitive or critical systems.

domains.name: User devices
domains.description: Endpoints issued to the workforce, including desktops and laptops.
domains.risk_context: Widespread use and exposure make user devices common entry points for adversaries seeking access to the environment.

priority_phases.summary: Boundary services and Identity services are prioritised because they are common pathways for adversaries seeking initial access to an organisation’s environment. Weaknesses in these domains can enable unauthorised access and undermine security controls elsewhere in the environment. Addressing them together strengthens the protection of external access pathways and the identities used to access systems and services.

Privileged environments can provide adversaries with elevated access following an intrusion. Critical processes and services are prioritised because their compromise or disruption could have significant consequences for an organisation. Addressing these domains together reduces the likelihood that an adversary can escalate access and affect systems and services that are critical to organisational outcomes.

Business systems and User devices are widely distributed across enterprise IT environments and are common targets for adversaries. They are addressed after the earlier phases so organisations can build on the protections established for boundary, identity, privileged and critical environments. This sequencing helps reduce the likelihood that compromise of a business system or user device can spread across the organisation’s environment.

domains.name: Governance and culture
domains.description: Policies, risk management processes, roles and security culture that underpin cyber security program.
domains.risk_context: Unclear ownership and accountability can lead to inconsistent security decisions and outcomes degrading over time.

domains.name: Visibility and response
domains.description: Procedures and capabilities for detecting, analysing and responding to cyber security events and incidents. In OT, visibility often has a second use in engineering fault analysis.
domains.risk_context: Limited visibility and response can delay the detection, analysis and containment of intrusions. In OT, this could lead to potentially catastrophic system failure.

domains.name: Critical processes and services
domains.description: Core systems and networks which are essential to safely deliver the product or service for which an organisation exists.
domains.risk_context: Compromise or loss of these systems can disrupt the organisation’s ability to deliver critical outcomes or services.

domains.name: Boundary services
domains.description: Assets at network boundaries that broker connectivity between environments of different trust levels, including internet-facing services, edge devices and points of connection to other OT systems.
domains.risk_context: Internet-facing and boundary services may be routinely exposed to adversary scanning and exploitation making them common targets for initial access.

domains.name: Identity services
domains.description: Identity, credential and access management services such as directories, authentication and authorisation services or credential stores.
domains.risk_context: Compromise of identity services can enable an adversary to gain persistent or privileged access across the enterprise.

domains.name: Privileged environments
domains.description: Systems, services and devices that support privileged activities, management services and high-impact administrative functions. Within OT, this includes items which, in an enterprise IT context, would be considered user or endpoint devices.
domains.risk_context: Compromise of privileged systems can give an adversary extensive control over systems, services and security controls. Within OT, any device with connectivity within a privileged environment must be considered a privileged device.

domains.name: Business systems
domains.description: Supporting enterprise functions that collectively enable organisational operations.
domains.risk_context: Compromise can disrupt day-to-day operations and provide pathways to more sensitive or critical systems. Business systems may exist within the IT systems of an organisation, with their OT process support possibly making them considered part of the OT systems.

domains.name: User devices
domains.description: Endpoints issued to the workforce, including desktops and laptops.
domains.risk_context: The critical nature of OT systems, coupled with the high-risk cyber security possibilities present in many environments, should prohibit the use of typically configured end-user or endpoint devices within OT environments. Use of such devices risks the unintended introduction of cyber threats directly into the privileged OT environment. All devices within the OT system must be considered as privileged and treated accordingly.

priority_phases.summary: Boundary services are prioritised because they provide pathways between OT systems and external or less trusted environments. Critical processes and services are prioritised because their compromise or disruption could have significant safety, operational, environmental or service-delivery consequences. Addressing these domains together strengthens the protection of pathways into the OT environment while protecting the systems and processes with the greatest potential consequence.

Privileged environments and Identity services control administrative and privileged access to OT systems. Weaknesses in these domains can allow an adversary to gain elevated access, move through the environment or make unauthorised changes to critical systems and processes. Addressing these domains together reduces the likelihood that an initial compromise can escalate.

Business systems are addressed after the domains that protect critical operations, connectivity and privileged access. This sequencing reduces the likelihood that compromise of a business system can provide a pathway to critical OT systems while strengthening the protection of business functions that support OT operations.

actions.action: Formally define and establish executive and board-level accountabilities for OT cyber security, including setting, monitoring and adjusting organisational risk appetite, and review these accountabilities at a defined cadence.
Establish and maintain executive accountability for the use, governance and risk management of artificial intelligence within the organisation.

Assign sufficient cyber security personnel and resources with the required skills to operate, monitor, maintain and manage the lifecycle of controls across OT, and define cyber security responsibilities within role descriptions.

Protect OT system information, and the systems outside the OT environment that are critical to OT functionality, as high-value assets, and prevent public disclosure of OT device installation details, requiring third parties to do the same.

Establish and maintain a process to assess and manage supply chain risk for hardware, software and third party service providers, and to confirm that providers of services essential to OT understand the criticality of vital OT and can meet agreed levels of prioritised support.

Establish and maintain a process for identifying, assessing and managing the cyber security risk associated with legacy and unsupported systems that remain operationally critical, until they can be removed or replaced.

Conduct regular exercises of isolation and sustained isolated operation, covering isolation decision-making, threat hunting before reconnection, safe removal of isolation, sustained operation for the defined isolation period, artefact capture, and staff movement in a degraded communications environment.
Notify local operators of authorised remote maintenance or supplier activity, so that unexpected changes are not normalised or ignored.

Ensure all personnel receive cyber security awareness training that is tailored to how they will interact with OT systems in their assigned roles, and update it on a regular basis to reflect current threats and operational considerations.

Use an approved asset inventory mechanism that supports automated discovery to detect new and changed assets, recording physical and logical location, role, criticality, dependencies, known vulnerabilities and existing compensating controls.
Identify and document vital OT, and the enabling systems and services on which vital OT depends, including those located outside the OT environment.
Identify and analyse the OT attack surface, security boundaries and connectivity, including the points through which complete isolation can be enacted, and review these inputs on a continuous basis.
Update business and operational continuity plans to reflect the impact that isolation will have on business and operational processes.

Maintain alternative communications for site-to-site and site-to-staff use during degradation or loss of normal communications, and establish processes to have the right staff at the right site when isolation is enacted.
Establish, maintain and exercise a plan to rapidly disconnect remote access when malicious activity is identified.
Establish and maintain an effective process, independent of systems outside the OT environment, for personnel to raise an OT cyber security concern.

Maintain the capability to recover, without supplier support, any system that cannot acceptably remain offline, at least to a minimum viable level of service, including a plan to replace key OT devices following destructive attacks.
